variants.name: recall-then-match (instruction-only)
variants.technique: Recall-then-match (self-generated knowledge / step-back derivation, internal-only reasoning)
variants.change_vs_baseline: Inserts one new paragraph (after the bullet-principle list, before the retrieved-context paragraph) instructing the model to silently recall its own guideline-based answer BEFORE reading/comparing options, then match that recalled answer against a-d; if no option matches and the sentinel is present, pick the sentinel. Everything else — persona, principles, JSON schema, CITAS/IMAGENES blocks, question block — is verbatim from baseline. GIFT13 form additionally restores the {chunks}/{question} injection placeholders (absent from the current baseline file) per the GIFT13 authoring rules, and has the recall step explicitly draw on {chunks} first, falling back to parametric knowledge when chunks are empty/irrelevant.
variants.hypothesis: Deriving an answer independently before scanning the option list removes the option-relative 'closest distractor' comparison that causes anchoring (Zheng et al. 2023 Step-Back; Liu et al. 2022 Generated Knowledge). Because the recalled answer is fixed before options are read, absence of a match becomes the natural, low-effort trigger for the sentinel rather than an effortful override of a default 'pick something' behavior — this should raise Condition-B recall with minimal risk to Condition-A, since a correct listed option still matches the recalled answer and gets selected normally. In the GIFT13/RAG form, grounding the recall step in {chunks} first is expected to sharpen the match/no-match signal further (Nori et al. 2023 Medprompt retrieval+CoT synergy), making this the variant most likely to show a bigger lift once retrieval is live than on the no-RAG OpenRouter proxy.
variants.risks: If the model's independently recalled 'correct answer' is itself wrong (a genuine knowledge gap rather than a NOTA case), it may fail to match a genuinely correct listed option (paraphrased differently) and over-select the sentinel — mitigated only partially by instructing 'coincide en su contenido clínico' (substance match) rather than literal string match, but this is a real residual risk to monitor via Condition-A accuracy. In the GIFT13/RAG form, if {chunks} is present but incomplete (misses the fact supporting the true correct option), the recall step may anchor on an evidence-driven-but-wrong recollection and over-select the sentinel — a retrieval-recall failure masquerading as answer-absence, per the RAG-arm caution in the digest. Because output_mode is strict_json with no visible reasoning field, this recall step is unverifiable/un-auditable in the output — any errors in the internal recall cannot be inspected post hoc, only inferred from wrong answers.

variants.name: NOTA calibration (balanced)
variants.technique: Explicit balanced NOTA decision rule (symmetric abstain-clause / least-incorrect-vs-truly-correct framing, internal-only reasoning)
variants.change_vs_baseline: Inserts one new paragraph (same location as v01, after the bullet-principle list, before the retrieved-context paragraph) stating an explicit, symmetric decision rule for the «Ninguna de las respuestas anteriores es correcta.» option: select it ONLY when all three other options fail an absolute (not relative/'least-incorrect') correctness standard; explicitly forbid selecting it out of difficulty/uncertainty; explicitly forbid avoiding it when it is genuinely correct. No per-option verdict schema, no visible reasoning field, no recall-before-options step — this is a pure policy statement, isolating the effect of naming the rule versus v01's structural recall mechanism. GIFT13 form ties the same rule to {chunks} first with a parametric-knowledge fallback, and restores the {chunks}/{question} placeholders per the GIFT13 authoring rules.
variants.hypothesis: This targets the top-priority, cheapest lever identified across all four research clusters: the live prompt gives the sentinel zero policy, and both Tam et al. (2025) and Elhady et al./WiCkeD (2025) attribute the 12-50pp NOTA-specific accuracy drop to exactly this missing meta-cognitive rule, which generic CoT alone does not fix. Stating the rule explicitly and symmetrically (select only on absolute failure of A-D; do not avoid it when correct) should lift Condition-B recall by removing the default pretrained bias against NA-style options, while the explicit 'ni con más resistencia ni con menos' symmetry clause is designed to guard Condition-A precision — directly following the Abstain-QA framing and the WiCkeD/Abstention-artifact caution to pair every encouraging clause with a countervailing one.
variants.risks: Any explicit legitimization of the sentinel — even symmetrically worded — can shift selection rates in ways decoupled from genuine correctness ('LLM Abstention Can Be a Prompt Artifact,' arXiv:2507.16199): the model may over-select the sentinel on Condition-A items as a prompt artifact rather than genuine answer-absence detection, trading false negatives for false positives. Because this variant has no structural verification step (no per-option verdict, no recall-first derivation), it relies entirely on the model correctly applying an abstract rule during unobservable internal reasoning (strict_json, no visible razonamiento field) — if the rule is applied inconsistently, there is no way to audit why from the output alone. Must be validated against Condition-A accuracy as a guardrail metric, not Condition-B recall in isolation, per the digest's explicit recommendation across all four clusters.

variants.name: few-shot NOTA exemplars
variants.technique: Few-shot NOTA exemplars (Medprompt-style static demonstrations): two short worked examples appended before the real question — one where the correct option is absent (answer = 'Ninguna de las respuestas anteriores es correcta.'), one where a normal option is correct — each showing one line of reasoning then the exact 3-key JSON output.
variants.change_vs_baseline: Only addition vs. exp5_baseline_user_template.txt / exp5_baseline_prompt13_es.txt: a new 'EJEMPLOS RESUELTOS' block inserted after the REGLAS DE IMÁGENES rules and before the real question/chunks injection. Persona, principles, context-usage paragraph, JSON schema (still 3 keys), output requirements, and CITAS/IMAGENES blocks are verbatim from baseline. For the GIFT13 form, the standard 'Contexto medico recuperado:\n{chunks}' / 'Pregunta tipo test:\n{question}' injection block was appended at the end (per authoring rules) since it was absent from the read baseline file, and one sentence was added instructing the model to weigh {chunks} when available but fall back to clinical judgement when it is not.
variants.hypothesis: Per Nori et al. 2023 (Medprompt), pairing a few in-context worked examples with self-generated-style reasoning gives the model concrete precedent for actually selecting the sentinel with a full elimination trace, rather than defaulting to the nearest surviving distractor because it has never seen 'Ninguna' chosen before. Mixing one NOTA-correct exemplar with one normal-answer exemplar (both papers in the digest warn against 'always suspect the sentinel') should raise Condition-B recall without teaching a blanket bias toward NOTA, preserving Condition-A precision.
variants.risks: Exemplar surface-pattern leakage: with only 2 static exemplars the model may pattern-match on superficial cues (e.g. 'if the vignette mentions a first-line/gold-standard treatment not listed, pick Ninguna') rather than the underlying clinical logic, which could mis-generalize on Condition-A items that happen to share surface features with Exemplar 1. Also adds ~150-200 tokens/call latency and cost. For the GIFT13 form specifically, this baseline snapshot did not contain the {chunks}/{question} injection block, so I added it per the authoring-rule template pattern — this should be verified against the actual live server-stored prompt-13 before deployment, since the true injection point/formatting may differ slightly from what is reconstructed here.

variants.name: chain-of-thought (clinical)
variants.technique: Standard zero-shot-style deliberate clinical chain-of-thought: a leading 'razonamiento' JSON key in which the model reasons step by step about the key clinical clue and the four options before committing, plus one brief, generic reminder that the 'Ninguna' sentinel may be the correct answer. No per-option verdict schema, no step-back derivation, no evidence-support checklist — general CoT baseline only.
variants.change_vs_baseline: Only additions vs. baseline: (1) the output contract grows from 3 keys to 4, with 'razonamiento' (breve, en español) as the FIRST key, generated before selected_letter; (2) one instruction sentence telling the model to reason step by step in that field and keep it to 2-4 short sentences (per Wu et al. 2025 / Zhan et al. 2026 length-degradation caution in the digest); (3) one brief, non-mechanistic reminder sentence that 'Ninguna de las respuestas anteriores es correcta', when present, can be the correct answer. Persona, clinical principles, context-usage paragraph, CITAS/IMAGENES blocks, and the requirement to choose only among the four literal options are all verbatim from baseline. For the GIFT13 form, the reasoning instruction explicitly tells the model to weigh {chunks} inside its 'razonamiento' (rag=yes), and the standard 'Contexto medico recuperado:\n{chunks}' / 'Pregunta tipo test:\n{question}' injection block was appended at the end since it was absent from the read baseline file.
variants.hypothesis: This variant is the CoT-only baseline arm against which the more NOTA-specific techniques (explicit decision rule, per-option verification, step-back derivation) should be compared. Per Kojima et al. 2022 and Wang et al. 2023 (Plan-and-Solve), generic step-by-step reasoning gives modest general accuracy gains, but per Tam et al. 2025 and Elhady et al. 2025 (WiCkeD), bare CoT alone does NOT close the NOTA-specific gap — this variant is expected to show only a small or negligible lift on Condition-B recall relative to the strict_json baseline, serving as the scaffolding-only control that isolates how much of any observed gain in richer variants (v03 and later NOTA-specific ones) comes from reasoning structure alone versus the NOTA-specific machinery layered on top.
variants.risks: Per Wu et al. 2025 ('Why Chain of Thought Fails in Clinical Text Understanding'), longer reasoning traces correlate with worse clinical-QA accuracy in 86.3% of tested models — the 2-4 sentence cap mitigates but does not eliminate this risk if the model ignores the brevity instruction. Per WiCkeD/Tam et al., expect this variant to under-perform the more NOTA-specific variants on Condition-B recall since bare CoT does not target the meta-cognitive gap directly; it should not be read as evidence that CoT is unhelpful in general, only that it is insufficient alone for NOTA detection. Deployment-specific risk (GIFT13 form only): adding a 'razonamiento' key directly conflicts with prompt-13's existing 'sin explicaciones' / 'solo el objeto JSON' output-discipline language; shipping this cot_json variant requires relaxing prompt-13's server-side strict-JSON validation (which currently likely enforces exactly the 3-key schema) to accept and then strip/ignore the 4th 'razonamiento' key before downstream consumption.

variants.name: option elimination (per-option T/F)
variants.technique: Forced per-option verdict schema (POE, operationalized as a single JSON reasoning field) + explicit if-all-false-then-NOTA decision rule, evidence-grounded against {chunks} in the GIFT-13/RAG arm and against clinical-guideline judgement in the OpenRouter arm.
variants.change_vs_baseline: Added one principles-list bullet declaring the NOTA sentinel a valid, non-trick option; added a new paragraph before the output contract requiring a forced verdadera/falsa (OR arm) or respaldada/no-respaldada-against-{chunks} with clinical-judgement fallback (GIFT13 arm) verdict for each of the 4 options with a one-line justification, an explicit if-all-false-then-NOTA rule, and an explicit symmetric guard against picking NOTA when a real option is true; converted output_mode to cot_json by adding a leading 'razonamiento' key that must contain the 4 verdicts + conclusion; for GIFT13 added the {chunks} and {question} injection placeholders (absent from this baseline file) at the end, and reworded the question_id field description accordingly. Persona, principles order, CITAS/IMAGENES blocks, and the final question block/placeholders are otherwise untouched.
variants.hypothesis: Forcing an explicit, per-option verdadera/falsa (or respaldada/no-respaldada vs {chunks}) verdict for all four options before any final choice — combined with an explicit if-all-false-then-NOTA rule and a ban on selecting the 'least false' option — structurally blocks the anchoring shortcut where the model implicitly picks the closest surviving distractor without ever checking absolute correctness, so Condition-B recall on the sentinel should rise relative to baseline while Condition-A accuracy is preserved because a genuinely correct option will pass its own verdict cleanly. In the GIFT13/RAG arm, grounding the per-option verdict in {chunks} when relevant is expected to give the larger lift of the two arms, since 'not supported by retrieved text' is a cleaner signal than 'not remembered from parametric knowledge.'
variants.risks: (1) Balepur et al. (2023) found elimination/argue-against-wrong-answers reasoning can underperform direct answering via misaligned rationales; mitigated here by using evidential 'verdadera/falsa' or 'respaldada/no respaldada' framing rather than 'why is this wrong' argumentation, but residual risk remains. (2) Any explicit legitimization of the sentinel can itself induce over-selection (LLM Abstention Can Be a Prompt Artifact, arXiv:2507.16199) — must monitor Condition-A false-NOTA-selection rate as a guardrail, not just Condition-B recall. (3) For the GIFT13/RAG arm specifically, if {chunks} misses the passage supporting the true correct option (a retrieval-recall failure, not a genuine NOTA case), the option will be wrongly marked 'no respaldada' and the model may over-select NOTA — this is a retrieval-quality confound, not a prompt-wording flaw, and should be tracked jointly with retrieval metrics. (4) Adds ~4 short justification lines of output length per Wu et al. (2025)'s finding that longer clinical-CoT traces correlate with degraded accuracy — kept to one sentence per option to bound this. (5) Deploying the cot_json version against GIFT prompt-13 requires relaxing prompt-13's server-side 'solo el objeto JSON' clause so the leading 'razonamiento' key is not stripped/rejected.

variants.name: recall-then-match (visible CoT)
variants.technique: Step-back / generated-knowledge independent derivation ('recall-then-match'): the model states the guideline-correct answer BEFORE reading the option list, then matches that independent answer against a-d; if no option matches, it selects the NOTA sentinel. Visible-CoT sibling of a hidden-reasoning v01 variant, grounded against {chunks} (with clinical-judgement fallback) in the GIFT13/RAG arm.
variants.change_vs_baseline: Added the same NOTA-validity principles-list bullet as v05; added a new paragraph before the output contract requiring the model to state, in razonamiento, its own independently-derived guideline-correct answer BEFORE reading options a-d (grounded in {chunks} when relevant, with clinical-judgement fallback in the GIFT13 arm), then match that independent answer against a-d by clinical substance rather than surface similarity, falling through to NOTA only if no option matches; converted to cot_json with a leading 'razonamiento' key holding the independent answer + comparison + conclusion; for GIFT13 added the {chunks}/{question} placeholders at the end and reworded the question_id field description. Persona, principles order, CITAS/IMAGENES blocks, and the final question block/placeholders are otherwise untouched. Unlike v05 (per-option verdict table), v06 uses a single upfront independent-derivation step rather than 4 separate option verdicts — the minimal, visible-CoT complement to a hidden-reasoning step-back variant.
variants.hypothesis: Anchoring happens because the model reasons from the option list inward, scanning for whichever surviving distractor looks closest to correct. Forcing the model to commit to an independently-derived answer BEFORE it reads the options removes that inward pull: the option list is then only used for a substance-match check against a fixed external target, so when the correct fact is genuinely absent from a-d (Condition B), no option matches and picking the NOTA sentinel becomes the structurally natural outcome rather than an effortful override of a default bias. In the GIFT13/RAG arm, grounding the independent-derivation step in {chunks} (context-faithful prompting) should sharpen the match/no-match signal further and is expected to be the larger of the two lifts, since retrieved-and-confirmed is a stronger reference point than parametric-recall-only.
variants.risks: (1) If the model's independently-derived answer is itself wrong (a genuine knowledge gap rather than a NOTA case), it may mismatch a correct listed option and over-select NOTA — the match criterion is explicitly framed as 'same clinical substance,' not literal string match, to reduce this, but residual risk remains, especially for paraphrased-but-correct options. (2) Adds output tokens/latency for the upfront recall step; per Wu et al. (2025), longer clinical reasoning traces correlate with degraded accuracy, so the recall statement is capped at 1-2 sentences. (3) In the GIFT13/RAG arm, if {chunks} is noisy or only tangentially relevant, grounding the independent answer in it can manufacture a wrong 'confirmed' target (over-interpreting weak textual overlap) and push the model away from a genuinely correct but differently-worded option — needs the fallback-to-clinical-judgement clause (present) and separate retrieval-quality monitoring, not evaluation in isolation. (4) Same general over-abstention risk as v05 (arXiv:2507.16199): must track Condition-A false-NOTA-selection rate as a guardrail alongside Condition-B recall. (5) Deploying the cot_json version against GIFT prompt-13 requires relaxing prompt-13's server-side 'solo el objeto JSON' clause so the leading 'razonamiento' key is not stripped/rejected.

variants.name: self-check / verify-revise
variants.technique: Self-check / verify-revise (draft -> anchoring/absence self-critique -> revised answer), grounded in {chunks} for the GIFT13 arm
variants.change_vs_baseline: Added: (1) one bullet establishing the sentinel as a first-class, non-trick option evaluated with equal rigor (explicit NOTA decision rule); (2) a mandatory 3-step 'razonamiento' scaffold - tentative answer, then a backward self-critique explicitly asking about answer-absence and anchoring-on-nearest-distractor, then a revised final answer; (3) output contract changed strict_json -> cot_json with 'razonamiento' as the first key; (4) for GIFT13 only, added the literal {chunks} and {question} injection blocks (absent from the baseline file) and tied the self-critique explicitly to whether {chunks} supports the tentative pick, falling back to medical judgement when chunks are empty/irrelevant. Persona, principios list, CITAS/IMAGENES blocks, and the final question block are otherwise verbatim.
variants.hypothesis: Backward self-verification (Weng et al. 2022) forces an explicit second look at the tentative pick before commitment, and naming the two exact failure modes (answer-absence, anchoring) inside the self-critique operationalizes the 'meta-cognitive gap' Tam et al. (2025) and WiCkeD (Elhady et al. 2025) attribute the NOTA drop to - generic CoT alone does not fix it, but a targeted critique question should. In the GIFT13/RAG arm, binding the critique to whether {chunks} actually supports the draft converts a vague plausibility judgment into a checkable grounding question, which should be the largest lift once retrieval is live (Nori et al. 2023 Medprompt synergy; Self-RAG-style grounding).
variants.risks: Symmetry risk: an aggressive self-critique can flip the model into over-selecting NOTA on Condition-A items with a genuinely correct option present (Abstain-QA / 'LLM Abstention Can Be a Prompt Artifact', arXiv:2507.16199) - must monitor Condition-A accuracy, not just Condition-B recall, as the guardrail metric. Retrieval-recall risk (GIFT13 arm only): if {chunks} misses the passage supporting the true correct option, step 2's grounding question will read as 'not supported' and drive a false NOTA pick - this is a retrieval bug masquerading as a genuine NOTA case and should be tracked separately from prompt-technique performance. Deploying the cot_json variant requires relaxing GIFT prompt-13's server-side 'solo el objeto JSON' clause so the added 'razonamiento' key is accepted rather than rejected as extra text.

variants.name: confidence / abstention framing
variants.technique: Confidence / abstention framing - calibrated three-tier confidence (alta/media/baja) routing to the sentinel; alta only for unambiguous, complete guideline match
variants.change_vs_baseline: Added: (1) one bullet naming the sentinel a first-class option, gated on a three-tier confidence definition rather than left with no policy; (2) a mandatory 2-3 step 'razonamiento' scaffold that (a) names the a-priori best clinical option, (b) assigns a strict alta/media/baja confidence label with explicit criteria for each tier, (c) applies a hard decision rule (only 'alta' keeps a lettered option; 'media' or 'baja' forces the sentinel, even when that option is still the best of the four); (3) output contract changed strict_json -> cot_json with 'razonamiento' first, required to state the confidence tier explicitly; (4) for GIFT13 only, added the literal {chunks}/{question} injection blocks and tied the confidence criteria to whether {chunks} supports the option, with an explicit fallback so empty/irrelevant chunks don't auto-downgrade confidence. Persona, principios list, CITAS/IMAGENES blocks, and the final question block are otherwise verbatim.
variants.hypothesis: This directly operationalizes the 'least-incorrect vs. truly-correct' distinction (arXiv:2402.01349) and the abstention-strategy literature (Madhusudhan et al. 2024, arXiv:2407.16221) as a calibrated routing rule: only the top confidence tier is allowed to keep a lettered option, so the model cannot select a merely-plausible/'least wrong' distractor at 'media' or 'baja' confidence - that band is hard-routed to the sentinel. This is stronger than open-ended verbalized-confidence gating (which the abstention literature found weak/miscalibrated) because the tiers are pre-defined by strict criteria (inequívoca+completa+sin matices erróneos) rather than left to the model's free-form self-rating, and it gives Condition-B recall a mechanical trigger rather than a vibe-based one.
variants.risks: Verbalized confidence is documented as poorly calibrated in general (arXiv:2410.04315) - even with strict tier definitions, the model's own alta/media/baja label is self-graded and could be optimistic (masking true uncertainty as 'alta', under-triggering NOTA) or conservative (over-triggering NOTA on genuinely correct-but-atypically-worded options), so this must be validated against ground truth, not trusted at face value. The 'media/baja -> forced NOTA' rule is more aggressive than v07's evaluative self-critique and carries a higher over-abstention risk per WiCkeD/Abstain-QA (arXiv:2507.16199) - Condition-A accuracy must be tracked as the primary guardrail. GIFT13/RAG-specific: downgrading confidence when {chunks} doesn't explicitly support an option conflates 'the retriever missed the passage' with 'the answer is genuinely absent' - the fallback clause mitigates but does not eliminate this, and retrieval-recall failures should be monitored as a separate metric from prompt performance. Deploying the cot_json variant requires relaxing GIFT prompt-13's server-side 'solo el objeto JSON' clause so the added 'razonamiento' key is accepted rather than rejected as extra text.

variants.name: RAG-grounded verification
variants.technique: RAG-grounded per-option verification (GIFT-endgame lever): recall/derive the guideline-correct clinical fact first, verify each option against it, and select the sentinel only if none matches — grounded in {chunks} on GIFT, degrading gracefully to best guideline knowledge on OpenRouter.
variants.change_vs_baseline: Persona, clinical principles, CITAS and IMAGENES blocks are byte-identical to baseline. Added one new block ('VERIFICACIÓN GUIADA POR EVIDENCIA') with a 4-step reasoning recipe: (1) derive the reference clinical fact — from {chunks} on GIFT / from guideline knowledge on OR — before reading options in detail, (2) verify each of a-d against that fact with a 'coincide/no coincide' verdict, (3) an explicit symmetric NOTA decision rule ('Ninguna' is valid iff nothing matches; picking the closest-but-wrong option or over-selecting NOTA when a match exists are both errors), (4) a brevity cap. JSON schema grew from 3 keys to 4, with a new leading 'razonamiento' string key (cot_json). GIFT form additionally: rewords the context-usage paragraph to point at the retrieval block ('a continuación'), keeps {chunks} and {question} each exactly once in a new terminal 'Contexto médico recuperado:'/'Pregunta tipo test:' block, and step 1-2 explicitly bind to that retrieved context with an insufficient/irrelevant fallback to guideline knowledge — matching the DESIGN.md v09 spec.
variants.hypothesis: On GIFT (chunks populated), grounding the reference fact and the per-option verification directly in retrieved evidence should give the largest Condition-B recall lift of the OR/GIFT-13 shared-technique family, per Nori et al. (2023) and Liévin et al. (2024)'s reported retrieval+CoT synergy on medical MCQ and per the context-faithful-grounding literature (Zhou et al. 2023) — 'not supported by {chunks}' is a cleaner, checkable answer-absence signal than 'not remembered.' On OpenRouter (no chunks), the same recall-then-verify structure should still lift Condition-B recall via the step-back/independent-derivation mechanism (Zheng et al. 2023) plus the explicit symmetric decision rule (Tam et al. 2025; WiCkeD/Elhady et al. 2025), though the effect should be visibly smaller than on GIFT since it lacks a checkable evidence source — the OR run is expected to look weaker than the eventual GIFT result, as stated in DESIGN.md.
variants.risks: Retrieval-recall failure masquerading as answer-absence: if {chunks} misses the passage supporting the true correct option, the model will confidently mark it 'no coincide' and over-select Ninguna — a retrieval bug, not a genuine NOTA case; monitor Condition-A accuracy/over-NOTA rate on GIFT as a guardrail, separate from retrieval-quality metrics. Symmetry risk: an aggressively worded decision rule can flip the model into over-selecting NOTA on Condition-A items where a real answer is present (mitigated here by the explicit 'both errors are equally serious' clause, but must be validated empirically). Deploying the cot_json output on GIFT prompt-13 requires relaxing prompt-13's server-side 'solo el objeto JSON' enforcement clause to permit the leading 'razonamiento' key — this is an infra/config change, not just a prompt-text change.

variants.name: stacked best-of
variants.technique: Stacked best-of: step-back independent recall + absolute per-option process-of-elimination (POE) verdict + symmetric NOTA decision rule, in one bounded 3-step reasoning scaffold; GIFT form additionally grounds steps 1-2 in {chunks} with a guideline-knowledge fallback.
variants.change_vs_baseline: Persona, clinical principles, CITAS and IMAGENES blocks are byte-identical to baseline. Replaces the single-check v09 block with 'RAZONAMIENTO ESTRUCTURADO EN TRES PASOS': (1) RECUERDO INDEPENDIENTE — state the guideline-correct answer before scanning options (step-back/anti-anchoring), (2) VEREDICTO POR OPCIÓN — an absolute, non-relative correcta/incorrecta verdict with one-line justification for each of a-d, explicitly forbidding relative/'least-incorrect' comparison, (3) REGLA DE DECISIÓN (balanceada) — if all four are 'incorrecta' -> Ninguna; if any is 'correcta' -> pick it; both selection errors named as equally serious. JSON schema grows from 3 to 4 keys with a leading 'razonamiento' key (cot_json), capped at 3-6 short sentences to counter the length-degradation risk documented for clinical CoT. GIFT form additionally renames steps 1-2 to 'GROUNDED' variants that bind recall and each option's verdict to {chunks} first (contradice/respalda/no menciona framing) with an explicit fallback to guideline knowledge when the context is insufficient or irrelevant, and keeps {chunks}/{question} each exactly once in the terminal injection block — matching DESIGN.md's 'GIFT form additionally grounds steps 1-2 in {chunks}' spec for the ceiling variant.
variants.hypothesis: This is the ceiling variant: it combines the three highest-leverage single-call levers converging across all five research clusters — (a) step-back/independent-derivation before reading options, the mechanism-level fix for anchoring (Zheng et al. 2023); (b) absolute per-option POE verdicts rather than relative ranking, directly targeting the 'least-incorrect-option' selection mechanism documented by Wang et al./arXiv:2402.01349; and (c) an explicit symmetric decision rule, the top-priority fix identified by Tam et al. (2025) and WiCkeD/Elhady et al. (2025) for the meta-cognitive NOTA gap. Expect it to produce the largest Condition-B recall lift among the OR-arm variants in this batch, and — once {chunks} grounds steps 1-2 on GIFT — the single largest combined lift overall, consistent with Medprompt/Nori et al. (2023)'s finding that retrieval and structured reasoning are synergistic on medical MCQ.
variants.risks: Longest reasoning trace of the batch: Wu et al. (2025, 95 models/87 clinical tasks) found reasoning-trace length correlates negatively with clinical-QA accuracy (86.3% of models degraded under CoT) — mitigated here with an explicit one-sentence-per-step/option cap, but this is the variant most exposed to that failure mode if the model ignores the brevity instruction. Per-option elimination reasoning can underperform direct/confirmation-style answering per Balepur et al. (2023, 'It's Not Easy Being Wrong') when framed as arguing why an option is wrong; mitigated by using an absolute correcta/incorrecta verdict plus a one-line factual justification rather than adversarial 'refute this option' framing, but should still be monitored. On GIFT, same retrieval-recall-failure risk as v09 (a missing chunk can make a genuinely correct option look 'no respaldada,' driving false NOTA selection) — track Condition-A over-NOTA rate as a guardrail. Deploying the cot_json output on GIFT prompt-13 requires relaxing prompt-13's server-side 'solo el objeto JSON' enforcement clause to permit the leading 'razonamiento' key.

variants.name: mix: v03 few-shot + v10 stacked reasoning
variants.technique: Proper integration of the two genuine winners: v10's 3-step reasoning scaffold (independent recall -> absolute per-option verdict -> balanced NOTA rule) PLUS v03's two balanced worked exemplars, rewritten to demonstrate the 4-key cot output (razonamiento walking the 3 steps). cot_json.
variants.change_vs_baseline: = v10 (reasoning scaffold + 4-key output) with v03's EJEMPLOS RESUELTOS block appended, exemplars converted to show the razonamiento; one exemplar is sentinel-correct, one is normal-correct (balance preserved).
variants.hypothesis: If 'showing' (few-shot, v03) and 'telling' (reasoning scaffold, v10) are complementary, stacking should raise Condition-B beyond either alone while the shared balance keeps Condition-A intact (net > max(v03,v10)). If redundant, no additive gain.
variants.risks: Longest prompt (more latency/cost); mechanisms may be redundant not additive; cot_json GIFT form needs the prompt-13 server to accept a 4-key object.
variants.render_note: validated; RESULT B=15%(+10) A=55%(-15) net=-5 -> REGRESSED (did not sum). A-loss is CoT-degradation entirely in Gemma (6/10->3/10), not sentinel over-abstention; QA-verified. See RESULTS.md 'Mix experiment'.

result_summary.a_loss_mechanism: CoT-induced wrong-option errors, entirely Gemma; Qwen unchanged
